name: Ponte Vecchio
overview: Ponte Vecchio is a medieval stone bridge over the Arno River in Florence, famous for its shops built along it. It's one of the few bridges in Florence to survive World War II and is considered one of the most romantic spots in the city.
history: This 'Old Bridge' is a survivor of history and romance! The current stone bridge replaced several wooden predecessors destroyed by floods, with the last great flood in 1333 carrying away everything except this sturdy structure. Originally lined with butcher shops (the Arno River conveniently carried away waste), the powerful Medici Grand Duke Ferdinand I found the smell offensive when crossing to his Palazzo Pitti. In 1593, he evicted the butchers and invited goldsmiths and jewelers instead - a tradition that continues 430 years later! The famous Vasari Corridor runs above the shops, allowing the Medici family to cross the river without mingling with commoners. During WWII, the Ponte Vecchio was the ONLY bridge in Florence spared from Nazi destruction - allegedly because Hitler found it too beautiful to destroy. Today, lovers attach 'love locks' to its sides, making it one of the world's most romantic spots.
highlights: Traditional jewelry and goldsmith shops lining both sides
Vasari Corridor - secret passage used by Medici family
Beautiful stone arches reflecting in the Arno River
Stunning sunset views from and of the bridge
tips: Visit early morning or evening for fewer crowds. The bridge is completely pedestrianized. Great photo opportunities from both ends and from other bridges nearby. The gold shops are authentic but expensive.
